# heim-mcp

> TypeScript library that serves tools over MCP (stdio) to small and local models: lenient with what a model sends, strict after that, every mistake one English sentence.

## API

Every export of `heim-mcp` (see `src/index.ts`):

- `ToolError` — `class ToolError extends Error`; throw it from `call` when the mistake is one the model can fix; its message is the sentence the model reads.
- `ToolDef` (type) — `{ name: string; description: string; parameters: TObject; annotations?: ToolAnnotations; argAliases?: Record<string, string>; valueAliases?: Record<string, Record<string, string>> }`; one tool. `parameters` must be flat.
- `ToolAnnotations` (type) — `{ readOnlyHint?: boolean; destructiveHint?: boolean; idempotentHint?: boolean }`; published in `tools/list`.
- `ToolBackend` (type) — `{ tools(): readonly ToolDef[]; call(name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>): string | Promise<string> }`; `args` are already clean.
- `prepareArguments(tool: ToolDef, raw: unknown): Record<string, unknown>` — the validator on its own; throws `ToolError` with one sentence per problem.
- `assertFlat(tool: ToolDef): void` — throws a plain `Error` when any property is not a string, integer, number, boolean, or string enum.
- `createServer(backend: ToolBackend, info: { name: string; version: string }): Server` — the MCP `Server`; a duplicate tool name or a non-flat tool throws at startup.
- `serveStdio(backend: ToolBackend, info: { name: string; version: string }): Promise<void>` — `createServer` connected to stdio.
- `createDemoBackend(today: string): ToolBackend` — the in-memory household todo list with its fixture data.
- `FIXTURES` — the eight invented todos seeded into the demo.
- `FixtureTodo` (type) — `{ id: number; title: string; list: "home" | "shopping" | "garden"; due: string | null; done: boolean }`.
- `loadCases(path: string): CaseFileT` — reads and checks a case file; a bad file or duplicate id throws `Error("<path>: ...")`.
- `CaseFileT` (type) — `{ today: string; cases: EvalCase[] }`.
- `EvalCase` (type) — `{ id: string; message: string; calls: EvalCall[]; replay_only?: boolean }`.
- `EvalCall` (type) — `{ name: string; arguments: Record<string, unknown>; reply: string; error?: boolean }`.
- `connect(backend: ToolBackend): Promise<Client>` — an MCP `Client` joined to `createServer(backend, ...)` over the SDK's in-memory transport.
- `replayCase(backend: ToolBackend, c: EvalCase): Promise<string[]>` — runs a case through the demo server; returns one line per mismatch, empty when the case is golden.
- `runModelCase(client: Client, c: EvalCase, today: string, opts: ModelOptions): Promise<{ calls: { name: string; arguments: Record<string, unknown> }[]; answer: string }>` — drives a case through any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- `ModelOptions` (type) — `{ baseUrl: string; model: string; apiKey?: string; fetch: typeof fetch; maxSteps?: number }`.
- `matchCalls(expected: EvalCall[], actual: { name: string; arguments: Record<string, unknown> }[], tools: readonly ToolDef[]): string[]` — the call comparison. Both sides first go through `prepareArguments` for the tool of that name (so a call written with aliases and alias values matches a strict call; a tool whose name is missing, or whose arguments fail normalisation, is compared as written); an extra actual call of a read-only tool that no expected call names is ignored; then values are compared as trimmed, lowercased strings.

## Rules

Lenient in, strict after. `prepareArguments` normalises, in this order:

1. An argument that arrives as a JSON string is parsed; a non-object argument fails as `Invalid arguments: expected a JSON object.`
2. Arguments whose value is `null` are dropped.
3. Argument names are matched in any case; `argAliases` (alias → argument) are renamed first, and the real name wins over its alias.
4. `"3"` becomes `3` for an integer, `"true"`/`"false"` become booleans, `42` becomes `"42"` for a string.
5. Enum values match in any case, and through `valueAliases` (per argument, alias → value): `Groceries` and `boodschappen` become `shopping`.

Then the strict TypeBox schema runs; the schema the model sees in `tools/list` is unchanged by any of this.

- Arguments are flat: a `Tool.Object` of string, integer, number, boolean, or string-enum properties only. `createServer` throws at startup for a nested object or array.
- Every failure a model should read is returned as an MCP result with `isError: true` and one English sentence. A handler that throws becomes a JSON-RPC error instead, which the model never sees; throw `ToolError` for mistakes, and anything else is reported as `The tool '<name>' failed with an internal error.`
- Over stdio, stdout is the protocol: log to stderr only (`console.error`), with the tool name and the error's `name`, never an argument value or a reply.
- `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, and `idempotentHint` are published in `tools/list` when set on the tool.

## Error sentences

One sentence per problem, naming what is allowed:

- `Invalid arguments: not valid JSON.`
- `Invalid arguments: expected a JSON object.`
- `Missing argument 'title'.`
- `Argument 'id' must be an integer.`
- `Argument 'list' must be one of: home, shopping, garden.`
- `Unknown argument 'colour'. todo_add takes: title, list, due.`
- `Argument 'id' must be at least 1.`
- `Unknown tool 'todo_finish'. Tools: todo_add, todo_list, todo_done, todo_delete, todo_search.`
- `The tool 'todo_done' failed with an internal error.`
- `No todo #99. Use todo_list to see the ids.`
- `Argument 'due' must be a date as YYYY-MM-DD, 'today' or 'tomorrow'.`

## Demo tools

The demo is an in-memory household todo list; `createDemoBackend(today)` with `today` as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

- `todo_add` — parameters: `title` (string, required), `list` (one of `home`, `shopping`, `garden`, optional), `due` (optional; `YYYY-MM-DD`, `today` or `tomorrow`). Aliases: `text`/`name` → `title`, `date`/`when` → `due`, `category` → `list`; `groceries`/`boodschappen` → `shopping`, `house`/`thuis` → `home`, `tuin` → `garden`. Reply: `Added #9 'Milk' to shopping, due 2026-03-03.`
- `todo_list` — parameters: `list` (optional), `done` (boolean, optional, default false). Read-only. One line per todo: `#1 Buy dish soap (shopping, due 2026-03-02)`; `Nothing on the list.` when empty.
- `todo_done` — parameters: `id` (integer ≥ 1). Idempotent. Aliases: `todo_id`/`todo` → `id`. Replies: `Done: #1 'Buy dish soap'.`, `#6 'Replace hallway bulb' was already done.`
- `todo_delete` — parameters: `id` (integer ≥ 1). Destructive. Aliases: `todo_id`/`todo` → `id`. Reply: `Deleted #1 'Buy dish soap'.`
- `todo_search` — parameters: `query` (string). Read-only. Aliases: `q`/`text` → `query`. Case-insensitive title match; `Nothing matches 'x'.` when empty.

## Eval

A case file is `{ "today": "YYYY-MM-DD", "cases": [...] }`; each case is `{ "id", "message", "replay_only"?, "calls": [{ "name", "arguments", "reply", "error"? }] }`. `error: true` means the call should fail with `reply` as its error text. `replay_only: true` marks a case that replay mode runs but model mode skips. The shipped cases are in `eval/demo-cases.json`.

```json
{
  "today": "2026-03-02",
  "cases": [
    {
      "id": "add-with-alias-and-day-word",
      "message": "Put milk on the groceries, for tomorrow",
      "calls": [
        {
          "name": "todo_add",
          "arguments": { "text": "Milk", "list": "Groceries", "due": "tomorrow" },
          "reply": "Added #9 'Milk' to shopping, due 2026-03-03."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Replay mode runs each case against a fresh demo backend through an MCP client over an in-memory transport; no model, runs in CI:

```sh
npx -p heim-mcp heim-mcp-eval --replay
```

Model mode sends each message to an OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint with the tools from `tools/list`, then reports the calls the model made against the expected ones (`matchCalls` compares argument values as trimmed, lowercased strings). It compares each call after the validator's corrections, ignores extra read-only lookups, and skips cases marked `replay_only`. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` if the endpoint needs a key:

```sh
npx -p heim-mcp heim-mcp-eval --base-url http://localhost:8080/v1 --model qwen3-30b-a3b
```

Both modes print one line per case and exit non-zero on a failure. Replay mode's summary line is `<passed>/<total> cases`; model mode's is `<passed>/<scored> cases, <skipped> replay-only skipped`.
